source.title: Role of the basal ganglia in the control of purposive saccadic eye movements

confidence_rationale: Hikosaka's saccade work is the best-characterised single instance of the BG permission-gate in action, with electrophysiology: the SNr tonically inhibits the superior colliculus, the caudate disinhibits the SC to PERMIT a saccade, the STN/GPe can FURTHER enhance the SNr-SC inhibition (a No-Go strengthening), and -- crucially for ARC-107 -- the whole gate is strongly modulated by behavioural CONTEXT (working memory, expectation, attention, reward expectation). It grounds three ARC-107 components at once (permission-to-commit gate, STN-enhanced No-Go, context arbitration) and is the cleanest evidence that the gate is set by MORE than a single value scalar -- exactly the precondition MECH-448 needs. Held below 0.8 by modality specificity (oculomotor) and because reward-expectation FACILITATION of the rewarded saccade is itself a value-monopoly risk (the substrate can also collapse onto the high-value option), which is a double-edged grounding the mapping must flag.
failure_signatures: Hikosaka shows the SNr-SC permission gate is modulated by working memory, expectation, attention and reward -- multiple context channels gain access. But he ALSO shows reward expectation FACILITATES the rewarded saccade: if a single value signal dominates the caudate input, the gate preferentially opens for the high-value target and the others stay inhibited. This is the biological version of the F-monopoly: a context-modulated gate can STILL collapse onto one channel if that channel monopolises the disinhibiting input -- precisely the ceiling MECH-448 must break, now shown to exist in the substrate itself.

The gate's flexibility comes from the caudate carrying genuinely DIFFERENT context signals (memory vs attention vs reward), not one score. A REE permission gate fed only by F would reproduce the structure but none of the flexibility; the entry grounds the requirement that the eligibility/permission input be multi-channel, not the sufficiency of adding a gate.

STN/GPe can ENHANCE SNr-SC inhibition (strengthen No-Go); an over-active version is the over-braking / akinesia pole, while loss of it is premature/involuntary saccades (the impulsive pole). The same dual-direction failure ARC-107's psychiatric column tracks appears here in the oculomotor gate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The basal ganglia control saccades via sustained SNr inhibition of the superior colliculus; a purposive saccade requires selecting the right cortical signal, achieved by caudate-driven disinhibition of the SC (removing the SNr brake), with an additional GPe/STN mechanism that can further enhance the SNr-SC inhibition. The sensorimotor signals are strongly modulated by behavioural context -- working memory, expectation, attention -- and reward expectation facilitates the rewarded saccade.
mapping.ree_translation: Hikosaka 2000 is the worked, electrophysiologically-grounded instance of three ARC-107 components operating together: (1) the pallidal-like PERMISSION-TO-COMMIT gate (SNr tonic inhibition of SC, released by caudate disinhibition -- commitment as brake-release, grounding MECH-448's eligibility/permission framing); (2) STN-enhanced bounded NO-GO (GPe/STN strengthening SNr-SC inhibition -- the indirect/hyperdirect suppression MECH-449 generalises); and (3) CONTEXT ARBITRATION (the gate set by working memory / attention / expectation, the 'context arbitration' step in the design-note selection pipeline). It is the strongest single demonstration that the BG permission gate is set by MULTIPLE context channels, not one scalar -- the precondition ARC-107 says REE's selector lacks.
mapping.mapping_caveat: DOUBLE-EDGED grounding -- flag explicitly. Hikosaka also shows reward expectation FACILITATES the rewarded saccade, i.e. a value signal can preferentially open the gate for the high-value target. So the same paper that grounds 'multi-channel context arbitration' also shows the substrate CAN collapse onto a single dominant (reward) channel -- the biological analog of REE's F-monopoly. The entry therefore grounds the STRUCTURE (a context-modulated permission gate) and simultaneously documents the FAILURE MODE (value-monopoly at the gate) MECH-448 must break; it does not show that adding a gate is SUFFICIENT. Modality is oculomotor (saccades), one step removed from REE's abstract committed-action classes, so the transfer is functional. Literal SNr/SC tonic GABAergic inhibition has no REE counterpart (same divergence as Chevalier-Deniau).
mapping.source_context: Comprehensive Physiological Reviews synthesis of decades of primate single-unit recording in the caudate-SNr-SC oculomotor circuit during memory-guided and reward-biased saccade tasks; the most complete electrophysiological account of a BG permission gate.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (Physiological Reviews, primate electrophysiology, decades of work, definitive for the oculomotor BG circuit). Mapping fidelity good -- grounds three ARC-107 components together and directly evidences the multi-channel-gate precondition -- but discounted because the same data show a value-monopoly failure mode at the gate (double-edged). Transfer risk moderate: oculomotor modality + literal tonic inhibition -> abstract committed-action permission is a functional translation, not a 1:1 import.
